To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
in simian AIDS induced granulomatosis, local CD4+ T lymphocytes are increased, despite peripheral CD4+ depletion, and that endothelial VCAM-1 expression and lymphocyte division are enhanced.
the granulomas in simian AIDS are attenuated and are characterized by an enhanced local endothelial‐T lymphocyte signaling and lymphoproliferation, despite the low peripheral CD4 T cell counts.
granulomas induced by CFA in rhesus monkeys infected with SIV were grossly attenuated in size and contained a large population of proliferating lymphocytes, including CD4+ T cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the immune responses to SIV infection in rhesus monkeys and the development of a vaccine against HIV infection in humans.
the study of granulomas in SIV‐infection in rhesus macaques.
the pathogenesis of SIV infection in rhesus macaques.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SIV infection of rhesus monkeys results in a profound immunologic dysfunction, including an impaired granulomatous response.
granulomas in SIV‐macaques are attenuated in size and cellular composition.
the SIV‐infec‐ted monkeys developed a granulomatous reaction to the Freund's adjuvants that was attenuated compared to the control animals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SIV infection induces profound alterations in granulomatous inflammatory responses.
the granulomatous response is altered in SIV infection, with a reduction in the size and number of granulomas, but with increased numbers of activated lymphocytes within the lesions.
in simian AIDS granulomatous reactions are attenuated and characterized by an increase in lymphocyte division.
The main takeaway from our work is that

in simian AIDS (and presumably in human AIDS), there is an attenuated granulomatous response to antigenic challenge, but this is associated with enhanced local lymphocyte proliferation and adhesion molecule expression.
the SIV model is a good model for studying granulomatous diseases in humans.
the SIV model of AIDS in monkeys is an excellent model for studying the pathogenesis of AIDS.
